# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 83 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 83 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_083_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 6

**1** "What is the name of the Son of God?" I asked. "His name is great and boundless, and upholds the whole world. If then all creation is upheld by the Son of God, what do you think of those who are called by his name, who bear his name and walk in his commandments? **2** Do you see what kind of people he upholds? Those who bear his name with their whole heart. He became their foundation and bears them gladly, because they are not ashamed to bear his name." **3** I said to him, "Tell me the names of the virgins, and of those women clothed in the black garments." **4** He said, "Hear the names of the mightier virgins standing at the corners: the first is Faith, the second Continence, the third Power, the fourth Patience. The others standing between them are named Simplicity, Guilelessness, Holiness, Joyfulness, Truth, Understanding, Harmony, Love. **5** These names belong to those who bear the name of the Son of God and walk in his commandments." **6** "And the names of those carrying the black garments?" **7** "These also," he said, "are ten in number: Unbelief, Intemperance, Disobedience, Deceit, Sorrow, Wickedness, Licentiousness, Bitterness, Lying, Hatred. The servant of God who bears these names will see the kingdom of God but will not enter it." **8** "And the stones cast away that did not fit into the building — who are they?" **9** "These are those who believed and lived in a holy and righteous manner, but bore these evil names; they were therefore cast away from the tower and found unfit for the building. These harm those who walk in righteousness; therefore they were cast from the tower and given over to these women with the black garments, and they shall not enter the tower until they put away the works of these women."

---

*LOGOS lists all twelve virtues and ten vices precisely. "Bitterness" renders pikria; "Guilelessness" renders akeraiótēs.*
